correctness.rationale: Integer-polynomial proof: explicit Chebyshev transfer on every y^k; stable eight-adic jet invariant; three exhaustive seed families m≡2 mod4, m≡4 mod8, 8|m, including exact R2 derivative; induction adds exactly 3 valuation units and gives known mod-2 odd-square theta support. Every i and n within the stated domain is covered. Standalone exact modular checks: 10116 with 364 sharp odd squares. No finite test used as infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Saikia--Talukdar Conjecture 6.2 explicitly predicts all-even Chebyshev polynomial valuations but is unproved in the inspected September 2026 manuscript. The new stable jet invariant and its three exhaustive even-color base families prove it for all even m, yield a previously undetermined explicit c_m depending only on ν2(m), and identify all sharp odd-square indices. Adiga--Ranganatha 2018 already covers the two-color coefficient consequence for sufficiently large indices, which is explicitly excluded as separately new. Targeted published-finding corpus and published-source searches did not identify a covering all-even polynomial theorem. Tang 2026 full text and other inaccessible works remain residual risks, not affirmative NOT_COVERING claims.
residual_risks: Tang 2026 Springer manuscript is behind a subscription; the abstract was read but its full theorems could not be inspected because institutional access required human approval. No absence of coverage is certified.
Earlier 2018 congruences already imply the m=2 coefficient specialization at sufficiently large indices; value/novelty concerns the entire even-color conjecture and its polynomial proof.
Additional historical or unindexed mathematical results may contain implicit all-even reductions.

value.rationale: Resolves an explicit recently published all-even-color conjecture in full, providing a uniform structural polynomial invariant, exact depth intercept controlled by ν2(m), and a sharp odd-square support law. This supplies an infinite classification beyond finite numeric tests and beyond older two-color congruences; no paper-sized contribution is required.
